---
title: "Annotation-informed models"
format: html
---

Choose the annotation policy according to the parameter that annotations are
intended to control.

| Route | Policy | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `stblr_csr_annot(method = "sbayesc")` | `fixed_marker` | fixed marker-specific inclusion probabilities and variance scales |
| `stblr_csr_annot(method = "sbayesc")` | `group` | sampled low-dimensional group inclusion/variance parameters |
| `stblr_csr_annot(method = "sbayesc")` | `learned_logistic` | learned annotation coefficients for BayesC-like inclusion/variance priors |
| `stblr_csr_annot(method = "sbayesrc")` | `annotation_probit_stick` | annotation-dependent mixture-component probabilities |

ST block-eigen `sbayesrc` and individual-level BED `bayesrc` use their
documented annotation inputs. MT BayesRC/SBayesRC uses one probit-stick
component-probability model and global trait-pattern probabilities conditional
on non-null status.

Annotations require finite numeric values, unique column names, deterministic
column order, and exact marker alignment. External matrices need unique marker
row names. Preprocessing records intercept handling, binary/continuous column
types, centers, scales, and any row reordering.

`prior_component_probabilities` are annotation-driven prior probabilities;
`component_probabilities` are posterior marker allocation probabilities. They
answer different questions. Fixed marker priors are not formal marker-level
convergence traces; learned low-dimensional coefficients can be diagnosed in
extended mode.

`maf_effect_s` is independent of annotation policy. MAF-derived annotations may
coexist with it, but their possible overlap is recorded and should be assessed.

## Probit-stick intercept identification

BayesRC and SBayesRC now give every probit-stick intercept a proper normal
prior. Its default mean is the probit transform of the continuation probability
implied by the resolved global mixture, and its default standard deviation is
1. This is an intentional model change from the historical flat prior.

The prior is not initialization. Supplying `alpha_init` changes only the MCMC
starting state. Users can configure a scalar or stick-specific prior with
`annotation_intercept_prior`, for example
`list(distribution = "normal", mean = "initial_mixture", sd = 1)`.

The proper prior keeps the posterior finite when every eligible marker makes
the same stick decision. If no marker reaches a later stick, its coefficients
receive a prior-only update. Explicit `intercept_flat = TRUE` is retained only
for historical reference and fails for empty or completely separated sticks.

LD-operator approximation and annotation-prior identification are separate.
BED, exact or approximate CSR, and retained block eigen use different data
likelihoods but the same annotation-prior kernel.

See [Annotation-informed methods](../methods/annotation_informed_models.qmd),
[SBayesRC annotation probabilities](../methods/sbayesrc_annotations.qmd), and
[MT BayesRC/SBayesRC](../methods/mt_bayesrc_sbayesrc.qmd).
